text: y2clerk exists quickly create formatted frequencies tables. leverages tidyverse, allowing user |> data frames, select() lists variables, group_by() others, include weights frequencies. three main functions y2clerk: freqs() - creates frequency table including ns percentages level variable list variables. freqs() flexible can also used calculating means, medians, quartiles including weighting variables. verbatims_y2() - creates table similar formatting freqs. However, function used string variables creates table responses given. cross_freqs() - creates frequency table similar cross tabs. group_var given function acts unique banner every variable listed freqs. Whereas group_by() |> freqs() produces set frequencies grouped single variable, cross_freqs() designed produce set frequencies grouped multiple different grouping variables one another combines results single dataframe.

text: freqs() multi_freqs() can return frequencies one variable single (optionally grouped) table – example, running freqs() several columns , running multi_freqs() "select apply" question stem made several checkbox columns. pivot_freqs() detects automatically checking variable column handles follows: Unique labels across variables (common multi-select case, checkbox item distinct label, e.g. "Basketball", "Football", ...): label used directly pivoted column name, exactly single variable. variable column dropped since adds information beyond label already conveys. Colliding labels across variables (e.g. several yes/questions share labels "Yes"/"", several Likert-scale questions share scale labels): using label alone column name cause different questions' values overwrite pivot. pivot_freqs() detects checking whether label value appears one variable, builds compound column names form variable_label (e.g. q_festivals_1_Yes, q_parades_1_Yes) instead. pivoting group_var case, variable kept additional id column (alongside label) rows different questions remain distinguishable.
